title: Germany’s apparel market remains under pressure
summary: Germany’s apparel market experienced notable pressure in 2026, driven by a broader contraction in European clothing imports and surging domestic energy costs. Provisional Eurostat data shows Germany’s...
content: Germany’s apparel market experienced notable pressure in 2026, driven by a broader contraction in European clothing imports and surging domestic energy costs. Provisional Eurostat data shows Germany’s clothing imports from non-EU suppliers fell 17.0% year-over-year in the first half of 2026. Figure: In fiscal year 2025–26, garment exports to Germany totaled $4.38 billion, highlighting the market’s ongoing scale. This downturn coincides with sharp cost increases across the German trade landscape. According to the Federal Statistical Office, import prices jumped 8.3% year-over-year in August 2026, marking the sharpest annual surge since December 2022. Export prices also climbed 4.7% during the same month. A 43.0% spike in imported energy costs served as the primary catalyst for these inflationary pressures. The weakening demand extends beyond Germany to the broader European market. Total EU apparel imports from global suppliers dropped 9.7% year-over-year to €41.1 billion during the first six months of 2026. Import volumes shrank by 6.4%, while average unit prices declined by 3.53%. Despite tightening market conditions, Germany maintains its position as a major European hub for international apparel trade. In fiscal year 2025–26, garment exports to Germany totaled $4.38 billion, highlighting the market’s ongoing scale. Moving forward, dynamic cost structures, shifting consumer demand, and fluctuating energy prices will remain critical factors shaping Germany’s global supply chains and trade stability.

content: Wendler Interlining Bangladesh Limited officially opened its new production facility in Bangladesh on Saturday, marking a significant milestone in the German textile specialist’s long-term commitment to the country’s ready-made garment (RMG) industry. The opening ceremony brought together senior executives of Wendler Interlining Group, industry stakeholders and business partners to celebrate the company’s growing presence in Bangladesh and its vision for the future of the global interlining market. Wendler Interlining, a family-owned German company with roots dating back to 1843, has evolved from a textile finisher into a specialist in high-quality interlinings for the garment industry. The company established its own Bangladesh subsidiary in 2022, building on its production presence in the country since 2009. According to the company, Bangladesh is a strategically important market because of its position as one of the world’s largest garment-producing countries. From 180 years of heritage to a new chapter in Bangladesh: Addressing the ceremony, Dr Gerhart Wendler, Chairman of Wendler Interlining Group, highlighted the company’s long history, its transformation through successive generations and its continuing commitment to innovation and quality. He spoke about Wendler’s journey from its establishment in 1843 to becoming an international specialist in interlinings. The company shifted its strategic focus to high-quality interlining fabrics in 1974 and subsequently expanded its presence across major garment-producing markets in Asia. Dr Wendler also outlined the group’s future ambition of strengthening its position as the market leader in interlinings, with Bangladesh playing an increasingly important role in that strategy. title: Rooftop solar offers a lifeline for Bangladesh RMG sector
summary: Bangladesh’s apparel sector is installing rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems to handle severe gas shortages and grid failures. Reliable electricity is necessary to protect export production. Rooftop so...
content: Bangladesh’s apparel sector is installing rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems to handle severe gas shortages and grid failures. Reliable electricity is necessary to protect export production. Rooftop solar helps factory owners produce clean energy, lower power costs, and run uninterrupted operations. Assessing industrial rooftop capacity and demand impact The potential for solar generation across the apparel manufacturing landscape is substantial. A detailed assessment by the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) reveals that 3,320 garment factories across the country possess a cumulative rooftop solar potential of 1,768 megawatt-peak (MWp). The study mapped roughly 9.7 million square meters of usable rooftop area. Under optimal setup, solar arrays can meet a median of 39.9% of electricity demand in large factories, 33.1% in medium-sized units, and 38% in small manufacturing facilities. Converting this potential into active capacity requires structured investment. Recent Report data identifies 509 factories as investment-ready, with another 1,359 factories capable of becoming investable with financial support. Installing rooftop systems across 2,303 non-solar factories requires an estimated total investment of $188.2 million. Expanding factory adoption and portfolio targets Factory-level solar deployments are expanding rapidly through experienced engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) providers. Solaric, a major industrial solar installer, reports a portfolio target of 212 MWp in total installations for 2025, which is projected to expand to 400 MWp by 2027. The Netherlands hosts major textile machine manufacturers like SPGPrints and Vandewiele Netherlands. These Dutch companies supply advanced technology for digital textile printing, carpet weaving, and yarn processing globally. Courtesy: Collected The Netherlands’ economy expanded 0.6% in the second quarter of 2026. According to Statistics Netherlands (CBS), higher exports and manufacturing output drove this overall economic growth. In addition, Dutch manufacturing output jumped 9.0% year-over-year in July 2026. This marks the strongest annual manufacturing gain for the country in four years, following a 5.0% increase in June. This machinery growth highlights rising capital investments by global textile manufacturers. Garment factory owners are buying more Dutch machinery for spinning, weaving, dyeing, and finishing operations. Stronger Dutch machinery trade confirms that supply chain partners are upgrading technology for late 2026 production.

content: Raidha Collections Ltd., one of the largest sister concerns of Labib Group, has appointed its new CEO, Shazia Zaheen Alamgir, daughter of Salahuddin Alamgir and Sultana Jahan, Chairman and Vice Chairman of Labib Group. She has been appointed Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Raidha Collections and has taken charge of the role. Shazia Zaheen Alamgir has been associated with the group’s business activities for a long time as Group Director. During her tenure as Director, she gained experience in Labib Group’s management and business operations. She completed her MYP diploma and IB diploma at International School Dhaka (ISD). She subsequently earned her undergraduate degree from Emerson College in Boston, USA, and her postgraduate degree from City St. george’s, University of London. In her new role, Shazia Zaheen Alamgir will lead overall business operations, with a strong focus on EU business and management of Raidha Collections. At the same time, she will work to further advance the company’s business growth and future initiatives. In her personal life, she is married to Siraajam Munir Khan. Both are associated with City, St George’s, University of London. Siraajam Munir Khan is the son of Ikram Ahmed Khan, Chairman of the Dubai- and Hong Kong-based Shun Shing Group. Labib Group and its associates extend their warm congratulations to Shazia Zaheen Alamgir and wish her continued success in her new role. title: Rampal power plant sets new record with 1,321MW generation
summary: The Rampal coal-fired power plant in Bagerhat has generated a record 1,321 megawatts (MW) of electricity, exceeding its combined installed capacity of 1,320MW. At around 4:30pm on October 3, Unit 1 g...
content: The Rampal coal-fired power plant in Bagerhat has generated a record 1,321 megawatts (MW) of electricity, exceeding its combined installed capacity of 1,320MW. At around 4:30pm on October 3, Unit 1 generated 656MW while Unit 2 produced 665MW, bringing the plant’s total generation to 1,321MW. Figure: At around 4:30pm on October 3, Unit 1 generated 656MW while Unit 2 produced 665MW, bringing the plant’s total generation to 1,321MW. According to Anwarul Azim, General Manager of the Rampal Thermal Power Plant, both units are supplying electricity directly to Bangladesh's national grid. “After production was temporarily suspended due to a mechanical fault, the two units are now generating electricity continuously,” he said. He added that electricity from the plant would be supplied to the national grid according to demand. The Rampal power plant, located in Bagerhat, was initiated as a joint venture between Bangladesh and India in 2010. The latest generation milestone comes after both units resumed operations following a mechanical fault, allowing the plant to supply electricity continuously to the national grid.

summary: BKMEA inaugurated its Water Cell yesterday (3 October 2026) to strengthen the industry’s role in responsible water management. The inauguration was held alongside an awareness and consultation session on Water Stewardship in Bangladesh’s knitwear sector. Organized jointly by WaterAid Bangladesh and BKMEA with support from the Embassy of Sweden in Dhaka, the program brought together […] The post BKMEA inaugurated its Water Cell to strengthen the industry’s role in responsible water management appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: BKMEA inaugurated its Water Cell yesterday (3 October 2026) to strengthen the industry’s role in responsible water management. The inauguration was held alongside an awareness and consultation session on Water Stewardship in Bangladesh’s knitwear sector. Organized jointly by WaterAid Bangladesh and BKMEA with support from the Embassy of Sweden in Dhaka, the program brought together representatives from the knitwear industry, BKMEA and international brands. BKMEA Director Engr. Md. Belayet Hossain represented BKMEA during the inaugural session. The day-long program featured technical discussions and group activities on measuring and reducing water consumption, increasing water reuse and preventing pollution, along with exploring opportunities to develop water-efficiency initiatives into viable and investment-ready projects. In his closing remarks, BKMEA Executive President Ehsan Fazlee Shamim emphasized that water management should not be viewed solely from a business perspective; it is also an ethical responsibility. He highlighted that the impacts of water misuse and pollution ultimately affect our country, communities and people, making responsible water use a collective responsibility. The initiative is expected to strengthen awareness, capacity and collaboration on responsible water management across Bangladesh’s knitwear sector. Khandakar Abdul Muktadir also said, the government is developing a plan in coordination with the JDPC and private-sector entrepreneurs to promote value addition across the jute industry. He said converting raw jute into products such as sliver, packaging materials and blended fibers could significantly increase its market value. According to the minister, a tone of raw jute, which reached around Tk150,000, or about $1,200, at peak market prices last year, could generate $2,400–2,500 when processed into packaging products. Notably, the value could rise further to around $4,000–5,000 per ton when jute is converted into higher-value products, including blended fibers made by combining jute with cotton or other fibers. The government aims to process the maximum possible share of domestically produced jute into value-added products, he said. content: With major investments in manufacturing, localisation, automation and R&D, Mallcom is strengthening its head-to-toe PPE portfolio to capture the structural growth of India’s and the global safety-equipment market Ajay Mall , Managing Director The personal protective equipment (PPE) industry is entering a period of structural growth, driven by industrialisation, infrastructure development, tighter workplace safety regulations and rising awareness of worker welfare. For Mallcom India Ltd., this changing environment is creating an opportunity to move beyond being a supplier of individual safety products and emerge as an integrated head-to-toe protection partner. The company has strengthened its manufacturing platform through its largest investment programme to date, while simultaneously expanding its product portfolio, localising previously imported products, introducing automation and accelerating R&D in advanced protective materials and technologies. Managing Director Ajay Mall believes the opportunity extends well beyond conventional market growth. In India and across the developing world, millions of workers continue to enter industrial environments without adequate protection. At the same time, occupational safety infrastructure is maturing, regulations are strengthening, compliance requirements are tightening and awareness is increasing. The formalisation of safety practices, implementation of BIS standards and expansion of organised supply chains are gradually creating a larger market for quality-certified PPE providers. In Bangladesh, the story of garments and textiles is […] The post Ten Years of Textile Focus: Telling the Story of Bangladesh’s Textile Industry appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Author: Sultan Mahmud Sohal, Country Manager, Corporate Responsibility, KM International GmbH (Branch office of FLORETT TEXTIL GmbH & Co. KG) Ten years is long enough to change an industry, and it is certainly long enough to leave an imprint on the people who work within it. In Bangladesh, the story of garments and textiles is often presented through export earnings, factory numbers, production capacity, employment and market share. These figures are important because they demonstrate the extraordinary scale of an industry that has become central to the country’s economy and international identity. Yet numbers alone cannot capture what this sector really represents. Behind every shipment is a worker beginning a shift, an engineer solving a production problem, a merchandiser managing a demanding deadline, an entrepreneur taking a financial risk, a technician learning a new machine, or a young professional trying to build a career in an industry that connects Bangladesh with consumers across the world. Behind every factory is a community, and behind every export figure are millions of individual stories. That human dimension is what makes Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry much more than an economic statistic. It is an important part of the country’s social and economic transformation, and for the past ten years, Textile Focus has been one of the dedicated platforms telling that story. content: Swiss textile machinery manufacturer Rieter has announced the appointment of Daniel Lippuner as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective November 1, 2026. The leadership transition follows the decision of current CEO Thomas Oetterli to step down on October 31, 2026, and hand over his responsibilities, including the chairmanship of the company’s Board of Directors. The separation of the CEO and Board Chairman roles had been planned since Oetterli took office. Figure: Daniel Lippuner new CEO of Rieter Leadership Transition & Board Governance To maintain distinct governance structures, long-standing Board member Carl Illi will serve as Chairman of Rieter’s Board of Directors until the next Annual General Meeting on April 14, 2027. Illi has been a member of the Board since 2017 and brings extensive textile industry expertise to the role. Outgoing CEO Thomas Oetterli noted that his departure comes following key operational milestones: “After the successful implementation of the Next Level performance program, the structural measures initiated to consolidate the sites and the acquisition of Barmag, the time has come to hand over responsibility to new hands.” Extensive Industry Experience Daniel Lippuner brings deep international leadership experience and technical industry expertise across spinning machinery, yarn processing, and textile components: Saurer Group: Former CEO. Oerlikon Textile Components: Former Head of Division. Heberlein Technology: Former Chairman of the Board and co-owner, maintaining close ties with the chemical fiber sector. Lippuner’s expertise in business transformation, operational leadership, quality management, and Asian markets will be crucial as Rieter shifts beyond its core short-staple fiber business. title: Sustainable composite buttons from textile waste
title_ko: 섬유 폐기물로 만든 지속 가능한 복합 단추
summary: A waste-to-value approach using cotton knit waste, wood sawdust and ETP sludge Introduction Buttons are small fastening devices commonly used in clothing and accessories to secure or decorate garments...
content: A waste-to-value approach using cotton knit waste, wood sawdust and ETP sludge Introduction Buttons are small fastening devices commonly used in clothing and accessories to secure or decorate garments. They are usually made from materials like plastic, metal, shell, wood, or resin. Plastic buttons, such as those made from ABS, polyester, and nylon, are popular because they are inexpensive, durable, and easy to design. However, these synthetic materials contribute to microplastic pollution, release harmful chemicals during production, and do not break down naturally. This raises serious environmental concerns [1]. With around 60 billion buttons produced each year, even a slight change to sustainable materials can significantly impact the environment [2] At the same time, the textile and fashion industries significantly harm the environment. They contribute to solid textile waste. Textile Solid Waste (TSW) is categorized into pre-consumer, production, and post-consumer waste. The textile sector generates nearly 5% of all global waste, while millions of tonnes of textile waste are generated and disposed of in landfills each year. [3]. This study explores making composite buttons using waste fabric, wood sawdust, and ETP sludge, with epoxy resin as the binder using the Hand Lay-Up method. Findings show that these waste-based composites could serve as a sustainable and functional alternative to traditional plastic buttons in the textile industry Objectives The goal of this project is to create sustainable composite buttons using leftover textiles and assess how well they work for real-world uses. title: Sedex expands supply chain mapping beyond Tier 1
summary: Sedex has upgraded its supply chain sustainability platform to give companies deeper visibility into suppliers beyond Tier 1. The update comes as companies face growing pressure to identify risks acr...
content: Sedex has upgraded its supply chain sustainability platform to give companies deeper visibility into suppliers beyond Tier 1. The update comes as companies face growing pressure to identify risks across extended supply chains. Sedex’s sample survey found that only 12% of organizations have data from most of their second-tier suppliers. Sedex data shows another gap. About 15% of supply chain worksites have no measures to ensure their suppliers or subcontractors meet required labor standards. The new mapping workflow allows suppliers to add and label upstream connections by tier. The platform also gives buying organizations more detailed risk intelligence. Analytics dashboards can identify higher-risk suppliers by tier and highlight gaps in risk mitigation. Sedex has expanded its risk assessment tools across 15 topics for more than 120,000 registered worksites. The Audit Risk pillar uses findings from more than 250,000 SMETA audits across 115,000 sites in 106 countries. It also incorporates data from the latest SMETA 7.0 standard. Sedex has also upgraded its Wages Risk pillar. It combines wage data from more than 70,000 site-level SMETA audits with external expert sources. A new environmental risk assessment feature brings environmental data together at the worksite level. This can help companies prioritize environmental due diligence across their supplier networks.

title: Patagonia joins ACT to push living wages across apparel supply chains
summary: Patagonia has joined the ACT Initiative, strengthening its focus on living wages through industry-wide collaboration and collective bargaining. Patagonia defines a living wage as income that allows w...
content: Patagonia has joined the ACT Initiative, strengthening its focus on living wages through industry-wide collaboration and collective bargaining. Patagonia defines a living wage as income that allows workers to meet basic needs such as food, housing, healthcare, and education. In many apparel-producing countries, statutory minimum wages remain below these levels. The company has worked on living wages for more than a decade. In 2015, Patagonia set a goal for all workers across its supply chain to earn a living wage by 2025. It also researched wage gaps, worked with suppliers, and introduced programs to support workers. These included supplier education, wage assessments, and Fair Trade mechanisms that provided direct financial benefits to workers. However, Patagonia now says broader economic and policy factors also shape wage outcomes. “For years, our focus was on the actions we could take directly with suppliers and their workers,” said Wendy Savage, Senior Director of Social Impact and Transparency at Patagonia. “What we’ve learned is that lasting wage growth depends on much broader systems, including government policies and industry-wide agreements.” The ACT Initiative, which stands for Action, Collaboration, Transformation, brings together brands, retailers, employer organizations, governments, and the IndustriALL Global Union. Patagonia’s move therefore shifts its living wage strategy from mainly supplier-level programs toward broader industry and country-level action.

content: Bangladesh's business and trade sectors are currently navigating various changes and challenges. The private sector is confronting a harsh reality shaped by factors such as the energy crisis, high interest rates, financing constraints, bureaucratic complexities, and the overall investment climate. Looming ahead are significant challenges, including graduation from the Least Developed Country (LDC) status, new trade agreements, the need to retain export markets, and the imperative to diversify products within the garment industry. Figure: Md. Fazlul Hoque, Administrator of the FBCCI and Managing Director of Plummy Fashions Ltd. Against this backdrop, Md. Fazlul Hoque, Administrator of the FBCCI, recently spoke with Textile Today. He is the Managing Director of Plummy Fashions Ltd. and previously served as the President of the BKMEA. He is also a member of the Board of Directors of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), Bangladesh. Drawing on his extensive experience in the business and industrial sectors, he discussed critical issues facing the country's trade and commerce, including the energy crisis, investment, LDC graduation, Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), diversification in the garment industry, worker wages, and FBCCI elections. title: Saurer Texparts holds technical symposium with Saiham Group in Bangladesh
summary: Saurer Texparts held an ‘In‑Mill Product’ symposium with Saiham Group in Habiganj, Bangladesh. The event brought 45 participants for technical training on its latest spinning components and solutions....
content: Saurer Texparts held an ‘In‑Mill Product’ symposium with Saiham Group in Habiganj, Bangladesh. The event brought 45 participants for technical training on its latest spinning components and solutions. The initiative highlighted Saurer Texparts’ focus on direct customer engagement and the practical application of technical knowledge in spinning mills. Led by M Gopi, Global Sales Manager, Saurer Textile Solutions Private Ltd ., the symposium provided participants with technical insights into solutions designed to improve energy efficiency, yarn quality and productivity in spinning operations. Among the technologies discussed was the Spinnfinity and E-Shape spindle, which can reduce energy consumption by up to 6%. The session also covered the PK 2360 SEH, featuring a robust mechanical system with a hexagonal support rod aimed at enhancing yarn quality in spinning machines. Another key solution presented was the RB 105 rotor bearing system, which uses advanced materials to support higher productivity in rotor spinning operations. The training was designed to move beyond theoretical product knowledge by demonstrating how the technologies can be assessed under actual mill conditions. Figure: M Gopi, Global Sales Manager, Saurer Textile Solutions Private Ltd . Following the symposium, Saiham Group is evaluating Texparts solutions in real production environments to assess their performance and suitability for its spinning operations. According to Saurer Texparts, the initiative created an opportunity for technical knowledge exchange while allowing the company to better understand customer requirements and support mills in improving operational performance. content: Design In Bangladesh Week 2026 will take place on 6-7 October 2026 at the United Convention Centre, Dhaka, bringing together Bangladesh’s fashion, textile, creative and business communities around a shared ambition: to create greater value through design. Supported by the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB), the first edition positions design as a strategic bridge between Bangladesh’s globally respected manufacturing strength and its emerging creative economy. The two-day programme will convene designers, manufacturers, exporters, entrepreneurs, students, academics, buyers, media and cultural stakeholders. Through runway presentations, designer exhibitions, conversations and professional exchange, the event will spotlight the people, ideas and partnerships shaping a more design-led future for Bangladesh. A first platform for a design led Bangladesh Bangladesh is recognised worldwide for its apparel manufacturing capability. Design In Bangladesh Week adds a new dimension to that story by foregrounding original design, contemporary craft, product development, cultural intelligence and brand-building. The platform is designed to help make Bangladesh not only a place where products are made, but a place where new fashion, material and creative ideas are developed and seen. The programme will feature the Designer Discovery Pavilion, a premium fashion exhibition and curated runway showcases. Emerging and established designers will have opportunities to present collections, explore contemporary interpretations of heritage, meet industry professionals and build visibility within the wider textile-apparel value chain. title: Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition targets scale-up of lower-carbon
summary: The Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition has launched with more than 60 fashion brands, retailers, manufacturers, and innovators to accelerate the commercial adoption of lower-carbon materials and product...
content: The Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition has launched with more than 60 fashion brands, retailers, manufacturers, and innovators to accelerate the commercial adoption of lower-carbon materials and production technologies. Figure: Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition will focus on organic, recycled, and next-generation fibers. The coalition was launched on September 23, 2026, by The Climate Pledge, Amazon, Stella McCartney and Canopy, with convening support from the World Economic Forum. It aims to address one of fashion’s biggest sustainability barriers. This moves proven solutions from small-scale innovation to commercial production. The initiative will focus on organic, recycled and next-generation fibers. It will also support manufacturing technologies that can reduce water use, chemical inputs and greenhouse gas emissions. According to Global Fashion Agenda and McKinsey, the fashion industry generated about 2.1 billion tons of greenhouse gas emissions in 2018. Around 70% came from upstream activities such as materials production, preparation and processing. The coalition is therefore targeting the supply chain earlier in the product lifecycle instead of focusing mainly on garment reuse, recycling and disposal. The initiative builds on the wider Climate Pledge network, which now includes more than 700 signatories across more than 60 industries. Its members are committed to reaching net-zero carbon by 2040. Fashion-focused participants include Anna Sui, Another Tomorrow, Bananatex, Brooks Running, Circ, DL1961, E.L.V Denim, Mother Denim, Selfridges, unspun and Vestiaire Collective. For fashion manufacturers, this could gradually expand access to lower-impact fibers and technologies beyond limited pilot projects.

content: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ Stakeholders’ Dialogue and Preparatory Workshop on Ending Digital Violence Against Women, held at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon, brought together policymakers, parliamentarians and civil society leaders to address the rapidly growing threat of AI-enabled harassment, abuse and exploitation of women and children. The session was moderated by Foreign Secretary Ambassador Asad Alam Siam, with remarks from Hon’ble State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ms. Shama Obaed Islam, MP; Hon’ble State Minister for Social Welfare Ms. Farzana Sharmin Putul, MP; Hon’ble Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Md. Asaduzzaman, MP; Barrister Jahrat Adib Chowdhury, MP; and Ms. Sanjida Islam Tulee, MP. Speaking at the dialogue, Vidiya Amrit Khan, Vice President, BGMEA, stressed that addressing digital and AI-facilitated violence must begin with a broader change in society, culture and mindset towards women. She highlighted the silence surrounding domestic and child sexual abuse, the social taboos that prevent survivors from seeking help, and the urgent need for stronger implementation of existing laws. She called for educating children from an early age to respect women and recognise their value, alongside stronger enforcement, AI safeguards and age-appropriate regulation of children’s access to social media. She further emphasised that, as a Muslim woman, she believes Islam unequivocally upholds the dignity, rights and respect of women. The meeting was part of Bangladesh government’s work to establish the Dhaka Dialogue, a government-led platform introduced at the 10th Dakar International Forum on Peace and Security in Africa on 20 April 2026. The government has decided to hand over the operation and maintenance of Chattogram Port’s New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) and its overflow yard (OCY) to a foreign operator. At a meeting of the […] The post Foreign operator to run Chattogram Port’s new mooring terminal appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: At a CCEA meeting on Thursday, the government gave final approval to a draft 15-year concession agreement with an international terminal operator. The government has decided to hand over the operation and maintenance of Chattogram Port’s New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) and its overflow yard (OCY) to a foreign operator. At a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) chaired by Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury on Thursday, final approval was given to a draft 15-year concession agreement with an international terminal operator. According to a proposal submitted by the Ministry of Shipping, Chattogram Port Authority (CPA) will sign the agreement under a project titled “Operation and Maintenance of Chattogram Port Authority’s New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) and Overflow Yard (OCY)” under a public-private partnership (PPP) project. Meanwhile, the CCEA gave in-principle approval to another proposal submitted by the industries ministry. Under the proposal, urea fertiliser will be imported from Russian fertiliser manufacturer JSC Shchekinoazot through a direct procurement method (DPM) via UAE-based Delta Star Trading FZ-LLC. content: From pioneering India’s Overhead Travelling Cleaner more than five decades ago to developing intelligent automation systems for modern spinning mills, ELGI Electric is now making automation the next major chapter in its engineering journey. V.S. Balasubramanian, President-Operations , ELGI Electric “Whenever we introduced a new product, we never compromised on technology. We first identified the best technology available anywhere in the world and then worked towards making it even better for Indian customers. That philosophy has remained unchanged throughout our journey.” This philosophy perhaps best explains both the longevity of ELGI Electric Industries Ltd. and the direction in which the Coimbatore-based engineering company is now heading. For more than six decades, ELGI Electric has built its reputation by identifying emerging technologies, adapting them to Indian textile manufacturing and continuously refining them in close collaboration with customers. Its pioneering introduction of the Overhead Travelling Cleaner (OHTC) to India established the company’s position in textile machinery. Subsequent developments in yarn conditioning, fire and metal detection and Bobbin Transportation Systems expanded that engineering base. Today, however, the opportunity is considerably larger. As textile manufacturing becomes increasingly automated, connected and data-driven, ELGI Electric is moving beyond individual machines towards integrated automation solutions that connect processes, reduce manual intervention and improve productivity. The shift is being driven by a fundamental change in the industry’s requirements. title_ko: 아윌미백, 우주글로벌과 중국 총판 계약…온·오프라인 유통 확대 추진
summary: 언노운네이처의 착색 케어 브랜드 아윌미백은 우주글로벌과 중국 총판 계약을 체결했다.아윌미백 측에 따르면 ‘뱀파이어 톤업 스프레이’는 지난 7월 중국 왕홍 따따의 라이브 방송에서 준비 물량이 약 2시간 만에 소진됐다. 브랜드는 해당 기간 더우인 주간 판매 1위를 기록했으며 이후 수만 개 단위 추가 물량을 현지에 공급했다고 밝혔다.우주글로벌은 지난 6월부터 해당 제품의 중국 물량 공급을 담당해 왔으며 이번 계약을 통해 공식 총판 역할을 맡는다. 양사는 온라인 판매를 중심으로 유통을 운영한 뒤 오프라인 채널까지 단계적으로 확대할 계획이다

summary: LG생활건강의 세탁 브랜드 ‘피지 모락셀라’는 2024년 7월부터 2026년 9월까지 출하 실적 기준 누적 매출 600억원을 기록했다고 밝혔다.브랜드 측 집계에 따르면 ‘모락셀라 세탁세제’는 쿠팡 전체 세탁세제 관련 카테고리에서 7월부터 9월까지 3개월 연속 판매 1위를 기록했다. ‘모락셀라 냄새제거부스터’의 누적 판매량은 5000만 알을 넘어섰다.기간별 매출도 증가했다. LG생활건강에 따르면 8월 16~31일 매출은 같은 달 1~15일보다 8.6% 늘었고, 9월 1~15일 매출은 8월 같은 기간보다 13% 증가했다.제품에는 자사

title: 석탄 연 500억·LNG 1천억 갑절
summary: 대구 염색 산업 단지(이사장 박광열)가 지역 주민들의 환경 오염 방지와 민원을 원천 해소하기 위해 열병합 발전소에 사용된 석탄 연료를 친환경 액화 천연가스(LNG)로 대체하기 위한 적극적인 방안을 서두르고 있다.특히 대구 염색 산단은 현재 사용 중인 발전용 석탄 연료를 LNG로 대체할 경우 소요 경비가 현재의 두 배인 1000억 원 규모에 달할 것에 대비중앙 정부와 지방 정부의 적극적인 재정 지원을 강구하는 방안을 적극 모색할 방침이다.대구 염색 산단은 최근 이사회를 열고 이 같은 친환경 연료 전환을 위한 타당성 조사를 실시키로 하

title_ko: 더퓨처, 1~3분기 글로벌본부 매출 전년 대비 841% 증가
summary: 더퓨처는 2026년 1~3분기 글로벌본부 매출이 전년 동기 대비 841% 증가했다고 밝혔다.회사 집계 기준 약 9.4배 수준으로, 국가별 제품 운영과 이커머스 채널 확대가 매출 증가에 영향을 미쳤다는 설명이다. 중국에서는 현지 소비자 수요를 반영한 제품과 마케팅을 운영하고 있으며 일본에서는 이너뷰티 브랜드 ‘낫띵베럴’을 중심으로 큐텐 등 이커머스 채널에서 판매하고 있다.미국에서는 틱톡샵을 활용한 판매와 콘텐츠 운영을 진행하고 있다. 항노화 뷰티 브랜드 EOA의 글로벌 플랫폼 입점도 단계적으로 추진한다. 내년 1월 ‘CES 2027’

title: 히어로즈 오브 코리아, 갤러리아 명품관서 향수·민화 결합 전시
summary: 향수 브랜드 히어로즈 오브 코리아는 10월 2일부터 15일까지 갤러리아백화점 명품관 WEST 5층에서 팝업스토어를 운영한다.이번 팝업은 향수 시향과 민화 전시를 결합했다. 히어로즈 오브 코리아의 향에서 연상되는 꽃과 문방사우 등 한국적 소재를 민화로 재해석했으며, 작품 제작에는 갤러리 일백헌이 참여했다. 특정 역사적 인물을 직접 묘사하기보다 조향사가 향으로 구성한 이야기를 작가가 시각적 이미지로 옮기는 방식이다.방문객은 향을 시향한 뒤 작품을 감상하고 다시 향을 경험할 수 있도록 공간을 구성했다. 브랜드는 이를 통해 후각 중심의 향

title: Six forces reweaving the future of global textiles
title_ko: 글로벌 섬유의 미래를 엮는 6가지 힘
summary: For decades, the global textile industry followed a simple formula: make more, make it faster and make it cheaper. That formula built enormous manufacturing hubs, expanded global sourcing networks and...
content: For decades, the global textile industry followed a simple formula: make more, make it faster and make it cheaper. That formula built enormous manufacturing hubs, expanded global sourcing networks and made polyester the workhorse of modern textiles. But the formula is changing. Global fiber production reached a record 132 million tons in 2024 , up from around 125 million tons in 2023. Production has more than doubled since 2000 and under business-as-usual conditions could reach approximately 169 million tons by 2030 . Courtesy: Collected The industry is being pushed to use different materials, reduce waste, automate production, prove its claims and build supply chains that can withstand disruption. Six forces are changing this transition: man-made fibers, circularity, AI and automation, traceability, supply-chain regionalization and advanced materials. Together, they are rewriting the economics of textiles. MMFs If one fiber defines the modern textile economy, it is polyester. Polyester represented around 59% of global fiber production in 2024 , with output rising from approximately 71 million tons in 2023 to about 78 million tons in 2024. Yet around 88% of polyester remained fossil-based . That creates one of the industry's biggest contradictions. Sustainability ambitions are growing while dependence on virgin synthetic materials continues to increase. Replacing polyester entirely is unlikely to happen quickly. Its durability, affordability, versatility and performance have made it indispensable across sportswear, outerwear, home textiles and everyday apparel. Then what will the next generation of polyester be made from? title: AI Labs Keep Demoing The Weirdest Fashion Use Cases
summary: The latest marketing push into always-on AI agents featured fashion, again. But the big labs keep showcasing brand-owners and professionals who seem to want to care less and delegate everything. The more useful promise is the ability to care more: freeing time and attention to improve the product. The post AI Labs Keep Demoing The Weirdest Fashion Use Cases appeared first on The Interline .
content: [Featured image using Dots artwork for inspiration.] Key Takeaways: For the second time in as many months, OpenAI has released a new product with a fashion workflow featured prominently in the accompanying demo. These hypothetical workflows keep presenting an odd window into the reality of AI deployments and the likely real sources of ROI for actual fashion businesses, and the incentives are difficult to decipher. Market data presented by a16z and The Interline’s own survey examine different aspects of AI uptake and measurement, with some correlation showing that AI adoption needs to translate into demonstrable product outcomes – especially if agentic commerce ends up de-emphasising website visits. In a new attempt at “sherlocking,” OpenAI launched its own virtual try-on service that hooks into its own in-app shopping experiences and into the company’s new play to become users’ default operating environment. title: Bangladesh exports rise 8.54% in September as RMG shipments recover
summary: Key insights September merchandise exports rose 8.54% year-on-year to $3.94 billion. RMG exports increased 8.56% to $3.08 billion, with both knitwear and woven garments posting annual growth. Septemb...
content: Key insights September merchandise exports rose 8.54% year-on-year to $3.94 billion. RMG exports increased 8.56% to $3.08 billion, with both knitwear and woven garments posting annual growth. September exports fell 11.11% from August, showing weaker month-on-month momentum. RMG accounted for about 78.30% of total export earnings in September. Jute, leather and home textiles added strength to the wider export basket. Figure: Export earnings rose 8.54% year-on-year to $3.94 billion from $3.63 billion in September 2025. Bangladesh’s merchandise exports maintained year-on-year growth in September, although export earnings declined sharply from the previous month. Export earnings rose 8.54% year-on-year to $3.94 billion from $3.63 billion in September 2025, according to the latest Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) data. RMG remains the main export engine Table 1. Bangladesh’s RMG export performance in September 2026 Category September 2025 ($ Billion) September 2026 ($ Billion) Growth Rate (YoY) Knitwear 1.86 2.02 +8.58% Woven garments 0.98 1.06 +8.54% Total RMG 2.84 3.08 +8.56% Total exports 3.63 3.94 +8.54% Source: Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) The RMG sector accounted for about 78.30% of Bangladesh’s total merchandise export earnings in September. RMG exports reached $3.08 billion, up 8.56% from $2.84 billion a year earlier. Within the sector, knitwear and woven garments both recorded year-on-year growth of 8.58% and 8.54%, respectively. The quarterly data also show that knitwear remained the larger apparel segment. During July-September, knitwear exports reached $5.96 billion, up 6.88%, while woven garment exports stood at $4.61 billion, representing 5.11% growth. content: HELSINKI – Global synthetic fibre production could have been almost half its current level without the rise of fast fashion. This is according to new research which used computer modelling to examine how the textile industry might otherwise have developed. Researchers estimate that synthetic fibre production in 2021 could have been 47 per cent lower without the growth associated with fast fashion. title: Rieter announces Daniel Lippuner as new CEO
summary: Swiss textile machinery manufacturer Rieter has announced Daniel Lippuner as its new CEO. The leadership transition happened as Thomas Oetterli is stepping down from the CEO role, effective October 31...
content: Swiss textile machinery manufacturer Rieter has announced Daniel Lippuner as its new CEO. The leadership transition happened as Thomas Oetterli is stepping down from the CEO role, effective October 31, 2026, and handing over the chairmanship of the company’s Board of Directors. Figure: Daniel Lippuner new CEO of Rieter Daniel Lippuner will become CEO of Rieter on November 1, 2026. He brings extensive international leadership experience and industry knowledge, particularly in textile machinery and components. Oetterli said the decision follows the successful implementation of Rieter’s Next Level performance program, structural measures to consolidate the company’s sites and the acquisition of Barmag. “After the successful implementation of the Next Level performance program, the structural measures initiated to consolidate the sites and the acquisition of Barmag, the time has come to hand over responsibility to new hands,” Oetterli said. The separation of the CEO and Board Chairman roles had been planned since Oetterli took office. Daniel previously served as CEO of the Saurer Group and headed Oerlikon Textile Components, where he was involved in businesses covering spinning machinery, yarn processing and textile components. He also served as Chairman of the Board and co-owner of Heberlein Technology, maintaining close ties with the chemical fiber industry. His experience in transformation, technology and quality management, operational leadership and Asian markets is expected to support Rieter as the company expands beyond its traditional short-staple fiber business. Carl Illi will serve as Chairman of Rieter’s Board of Directors until the company’s next Annual General Meeting on April 14, 2027. title: Is the biomass boiler boom creating Bangladesh’s next environmental problem?
summary: No gas, expensive diesel—Will our forests, soil, and air burn in the race for alternative fuels? Bangladesh’s industries, especially garments and textiles, face gas shortages, unreliable supplies,...
content: No gas, expensive diesel—Will our forests, soil, and air burn in the race for alternative fuels? Bangladesh’s industries, especially garments and textiles, face gas shortages, unreliable supplies, and rising energy costs. Diesel has risen from Tk 97.5 to Tk 135 per liter, natural gas costs Tk 26.09 per cubic meter excluding VAT, and LPG Tk 108 per kilogram. Many factories have already reduced production because of gas and electricity shortages. Entrepreneurs are therefore turning to LPG, diesel, and biomass boilers. But if we escape a fuel crisis by creating an environmental crisis, society will pay the price. Biomass: Solution or new crisis? Biomass boilers are spreading rapidly, especially chain-grate and fixed-grate models. Biomass could reduce fossil-fuel dependence if it uses sustainable agricultural and natural waste. The key question is: Do we have enough sustainable biomass? Installing a boiler is easy. Securing fuel for the next 10 years is much harder. Is rice husk enough? In Bangladesh, a huge amount of rice husk is used in rice bran oil manufacturing facilities and rice mills, where it is used for heating and steam generation. Biomass boilers had long been used in rice mills before being introduced to the textile industry in Bangladesh. Rice husk has a typical calorific value of about 3,000 kcal/kg, depending on its moisture content and composition. Due to its low calorific value, a huge quantity is required, which is not cost-effective. To increase the calorific value, they may mix rice husk with wood chips, sawdust, and wood. This raises a serious question: Where will the extra wood come from? Bangladesh’s forests are already under pressure. title: EURATEX calls for a harmonised EU framework for Extended Producer Responsibility
summary: EURATEX has joined a broad coalition of European industry organisations calling on the upcoming Circular Economy Act to establish a stronger and more harmonised EU framework for Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). In a joint position paper, the signatories underline that the Circular Economy Act should help Europe move from fragmented national waste management systems towards… Read more The post EURATEX calls for a harmonised EU framework for Extended Producer Responsibility appeared first on EURATEX .
content: EURATEX has joined a broad coalition of European industry organisations calling on the upcoming Circular Economy Act to establish a stronger and more harmonised EU framework for Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). In a joint position paper, the signatories underline that the Circular Economy Act should help Europe move from fragmented national waste management systems towards a functioning Single Market for secondary raw materials . Extended Producer Responsibility already plays a central role in financing the collection, sorting and recycling of waste across Europe. However, different national approaches and administrative requirements continue to create complexity for companies operating across borders and can limit the development of circular value chains. A more harmonised European approach The coalition therefore calls for a horizontal EU EPR Regulation , establishing a common baseline for EU-mandated EPR schemes while allowing sector-specific requirements where needed. Such an approach would help reduce regulatory fragmentation, provide greater legal certainty and support the scaling-up of circular business models and cross-border markets for secondary raw materials. The paper also stresses that EPR systems should remain producer-led . Producers should retain responsibility for decision-making alongside their obligation to finance end-of-life management, while public authorities provide appropriate oversight. Producer contributions should remain dedicated to the collection, sorting and recycling systems for which they were raised. Transparency, simpler rules and investment in recycling Greater transparency across the entire waste management chain is another key priority. content: Kraig Biocraft Laboratories has shipped its first commercial order of recombinant spider silk yarn, marking a significant step towards the use of the company’s technology in performance textiles. The custom-engineered yarn was produced to fulfil a purchase commitment from an unnamed global performance sports brand and will now be developed into a new performance textile. The shipment forms part of a confidential pilot development programme targeting the athletic apparel market. Kraig Labs said the yarn has been custom processed to the customer’s specifications, with the initial volume intentionally kept small for the precision application. “Completing the delivery of this spider silk yarn is a huge milestone for Kraig Labs,” said Kim Thompson, founder and CEO of Kraig Labs. “The volume is small by design. This is a precision application, not a bulk order.” Kraig Labs’ technology uses genetically engineered silkworms incorporating key spider silk proteins to produce recombinant spider silk. The company believes the resulting combination of strength, flexibility, toughness and low weight makes the material particularly suited to demanding performance applications. The commercial shipment follows the company’s work to move its spider silk technology from development and scaled production towards customer-led textile applications. Kraig Labs sees elite performance apparel as a potentially important proving ground for the technology, where improvements in strength-to-weight ratio, durability and other material properties can translate directly into product performance. “High-performance sport is where materials prove themselves,” Thompson said. “Performance wins. title_ko: Texverse 2.0은 10월 30일 BUTEX에서 개최됩니다
summary: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) will host the national competition ‘Texverse 2.0’ on October 30, bringing together students from universities, textile engineering colleges, and higher secondary institutions for competitions focused on research, innovation, creativity, and problem-solving. Organized by the BUTEX Science Club, the day-long event will begin at 8:00 am and continue until evening. […] The post Texverse 2.0 to be held at BUTEX on October 30 appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: The Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX) will host the national competition ‘Texverse 2.0’ on October 30, bringing together students from universities, textile engineering colleges, and higher secondary institutions for competitions focused on research, innovation, creativity, and problem-solving. Organized by the BUTEX Science Club, the day-long event will begin at 8:00 am and continue until evening. Different segments of the competition will be held at the university’s Auditorium, Seminar Room, Academic Building, and Central Field, while some competitions will be conducted online. The event has so far established collaboration with 25 student clubs and organizations from different universities and textile colleges across the country. These include KUET Textile Club, BUP Career Club, Textile Club-MBSTU, DUET Textile Career & Research Club, NITER Science Society, BUFT Career Development Club, Daffodil AI Club, Southeast University Textile Club (SEUTC), Green University Textile Club (GUTC), Sonargaon University Textile Club, and RTEC Research Club, among others. The competition aims to encourage students to engage in research and innovation while developing practical and sustainable solutions to challenges faced by the textile sector. It will also provide participants with a platform to showcase their creative ideas, technical knowledge, and problem-solving abilities. At the university level, the competition will feature project exhibition, research-based poster presentation, quiz competition, textile case competition, treasure hunt, essay writing and an artificial intelligence-based video-making competition. summary: The global Tencel fiber products market is expanding as apparel brands and textile manufacturers increase their use of lower-impact cellulosic fibers. According to Verified Market Reports, the market...
content: The global Tencel fiber products market is expanding as apparel brands and textile manufacturers increase their use of lower-impact cellulosic fibers. According to Verified Market Reports, the market was valued at $3.5 billion in 2025. It is projected to reach $6.15 billion by 2033, growing at a 7.8% CAGR from 2026 to 2033. The growth is supported by demand for sustainable materials, stronger traceability requirements and advances in fiber technology. Tencel products include Lyocell and Modal fibers, which are used across apparel, home textiles and technical applications. A separate 2026 market analysis gives a more detailed view of the fabric segment. According to PW Consulting, the Tencel fiber fabric market reached $3.67 billion in 2025 and could reach $5.94 billion by 2032, at a 7.15% CAGR. Lyocell fiber fabric held the largest share at 59.8%. Apparel remains the largest end-use segment. Apparel and clothing generated about $2.37 billion, or 64.7% of the Tencel fiber fabric market, in 2025. Home textiles followed with $927.7 million, or 25.3%. Technical textiles accounted for $365.4 million, or 10%. Asia-Pacific remains the largest regional market. It generated about $1.64 billion in Tencel fiber fabric revenue in 2025. Europe followed at $929.8 million, while North America reached $656.8 million. The broader fiber market also shows stronger demand for regenerated cellulose. According to Lenzing, global production of lyocell, modal, and viscose increased about 4% to 8.7 million tons in 2025. Lyocell and modal output increased at a double-digit rate. Technology remains a major differentiator. TENCEL™ Lyocell uses a closed-loop process that recovers more than 99.8% of the solvent. title: IFKT conference opens in Zagreb
summary: The 52nd International Conference of the International Federation of Knitting Technologists (IFKT) is taking place in Zagreb, Croatia, from 30 September to 2 October 2026, bringing together specialists from industry, academia and research. Organised by the Croatian section of IFKT in collaboration with the University of Zagreb, the international meeting combines technical presentations and poster […] The post IFKT conference opens in Zagreb appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: The 52nd International Conference of the International Federation of Knitting Technologists (IFKT) is taking place in Zagreb, Croatia, from 30 September to 2 October 2026, bringing together specialists from industry, academia and research. Organised by the Croatian section of IFKT in collaboration with the University of Zagreb, the international meeting combines technical presentations and poster sessions with opportunities for discussion and networking among knitting professionals. The conference programme began on Wednesday 30 September at the University of Zagreb Faculty of Textile Technology with a meeting of the IFKT Central Board followed by the organisation’s General Assembly. The technical conference programme opened on Thursday 1 October at Zagreb’s Nikola Tesla Technical Museum. Following registration and the opening ceremony, Zlatko Vrljičak delivered the introductory lecture, Employment in the Croatian Textile and Clothing Industry: With Special Emphasis on the Knitwear Industry . The first oral session focuses on technology, materials and characterisation and is chaired by Marcus O. Weber. Among the opening presentations is Cotton Grass Fibers – Textile Technological Approach , delivered by Marc Küperkoch. Thomas Mutschler and Marc Küperkoch are also presenting research into component optimisation for high-speed yarn guiding elements designed for processing highly abrasive yarns at high speeds. The work examines ceramic materials and high-frequency vibrations. The programme continues through 2 October, with the conference providing a platform for sharing developments in knitting technology, materials, textile engineering and associated research. content: DHAKA – Bangladesh is set to quadruple polyester-chip capacity at a local producer, in a bid to reduce reliance on imported synthetic textile inputs. The move comes as garment makers seek to expand beyond cotton and move into new product segments. The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has signed a US$50mloan with Modern Syntex Limited, part of TK Group, to expand its polyester-chip manufacturing operation in the Mirsarai Economic Zone near Chattogram. The project will increase the plant’s capacity from 107 tonnes to 407 tonnes a day. It is designed to produce high-intrinsic-viscosity polyester chips for higher-value textile and apparel applications, with commercial operations targeted for 2027. The investment comes as Bangladesh’s garment industry remains heavily weighted towards cotton, while manufacturers look to capture more orders for man-made-fibre products. Industry estimates put man-made-fibre apparel at about 25 per cent of Bangladesh’s garment export revenues, compared with around 70 per cent of global clothing consumption. Polyester demand in Bangladesh is estimated to be growing by about 10 per cent a year. The Business Standard reported in September that annual local demand is around 140,000–160,000 tonnes for polyester staple fibre, while demand for polyester yarn is estimated at 500,000–550,000 tonnes. The same report said Modern Syntex already produces polyester staple fibre, filament yarn and PET chips, and meets nearly 21% of the country’s demand for polyester products. It also reported that a significant share of domestic demand is still met through imports. The ADB-backed expansion is therefore part of a broader effort to build domestic capacity, rather than Bangladesh’s first move into polyester production. title_ko: Senbis 바이오플라스틱 연구원을 위한 Paul Schlack 상
summary: Momo Naeimirad of Netherlands-based Senbis Polymer Innovations has received the 2026 Paul Schlack Prize for research into the relationship between the performance and biodegradation of melt-spun bioplastic fibres. Presented at the 65th Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress held in Austria from September 16-18, the award recognised Naeimirad’s PolyBioDeg research into how the structure and properties of […] The post Paul Schlack Prize for Senbis bioplastics researcher appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Momo Naeimirad of Netherlands-based Senbis Polymer Innovations has received the 2026 Paul Schlack Prize for research into the relationship between the performance and biodegradation of melt-spun bioplastic fibres. Presented at the 65th Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress held in Austria from September 16-18, the award recognised Naeimirad’s PolyBioDeg research into how the structure and properties of melt-spun bioplastic fibres influence both their mechanical performance during use and their subsequent biodegradation. Naeimirad is affiliated with Senbis and the University of Amsterdam. The Paul Schlack Prize is one of the fibre industry’s longest-established awards for young researchers. First awarded in 1971 and named after Paul Schlack, the inventor of polyamide 6, it is intended to encourage research and development in the manufacture, processing and application of man-made fibres in Europe. The €3,000 prize is awarded annually at Dornbirn following assessment by an independent jury. Naeimirad’s work addresses an increasingly important challenge for biodegradable polymers – achieving the mechanical and processing performance required during a product’s useful life while ensuring that the material can subsequently biodegrade under appropriate environmental conditions. It is an issue closely related to the wider development programme of Senbis at its base in Emmen, the Netherlands. The company used Dornbirn’s Innovation Day and Forum to present its GreenPearls range of biodegradable compounds for fibre and filament production. The materials are being engineered specifically around individual fibre-forming processes, with the aim of overcoming some of the processing and performance limitations traditionally associated with biodegradable polymers. content: With its state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ranipet now fully operational, AMANN Group is moving into a new phase of growth in India—combining global thread expertise with local manufacturing, faster delivery, application support and a growing portfolio of sustainable and high-performance solutions. Sanjeev Grewal, Regional Business Director – Asia, Middle East & Pacific , Amann Group For AMANN Group, India is no longer simply another market in its global network. It is emerging as a strategically important manufacturing and consumption centre, with opportunities extending across apparel, home textiles, footwear, leather and technical applications. The German thread specialist, which began its Indian journey with a trading operation in Chennai in 2007, has now taken a significant step forward by establishing a modern manufacturing facility at Ranipet in Tamil Nadu. The transformation reflects AMANN’s confidence in the long-term potential of the Indian textile and allied industries. After spending years understanding the market, its customers and their requirements, the company commenced construction of the Ranipet plant in 2022. Commercial production began towards the end of 2024, following a two-year delay caused by the pandemic. The facility has since completed its ramp-up phase and is now fully equipped to serve the Indian market with AMANN’s portfolio of products. For Sanjeev Grewal, Regional Business Director – Asia, Middle East & Pacific, the manufacturing investment represents much more than localisation. It is a clear expression of AMANN’s long-term commitment to India. From Trading to Manufacturing AMANN’s Indian journey began with a trading company in Chennai. content: A robotic hand developed by Chinese firm Agilink has been taught foundational Suzhou embroidery techniques by master craftswoman Fu Xianghong, including separating silk threads, threading a needle, stretching fabric on an embroidery hoop and stitching. The demonstration puts a robotic hand to work with one of the most delicate and deformable materials it can encounter. A silk thread can bend, slip and change shape with slight changes in contact. Splitting silk requires one finger to separate individual strands while others maintain support and tension. Twisting thread meanwhile requires opposing fingertips to maintain contact while allowing the thread to turn. Threading a needle and stitching add further demands on positioning, force and coordination. The OmniHand 3 Ultra combines 21 active degrees of freedom with a fully direct-drive architecture and tactile sensing across the fingertips, finger pads and palm. Vision-based tactile sensors at each fingertip detect changes in the contact surface, providing feedback as the hand handles thin, deformable materials. “A single silk thread gives OmniHand 3 Ultra’s fingertip dexterity a visible measure,” said Qiao Tianjie, vice president of Agibot and CEO of Agilink. “It also reveals the possibility of handing more delicate work to machines.” The demonstration comes as Agilink reaches a new stage of commercial scale. Spun out from Agibot in January 2026, the company has shipped more than 15,000 dexterous hands to date. In August, its OmniHand series competed across all eight dexterous-hand events at the World Humanoid Robot Games, winning seven gold, four silver and three bronze medals. title: Urmi Group puts drivers' children's drawings on trucks to promote road safety
summary: Urmi Group has launched an initiative to make its drivers more careful on the road, placing drawings and short messages from drivers' children on the back of its goods-carrying vehicles. Garment facto...
content: Urmi Group has launched an initiative to make its drivers more careful on the road, placing drawings and short messages from drivers' children on the back of its goods-carrying vehicles. Garment factories and other industrial units use thousands of trucks, covered vans and pickups every day to move goods. According to 2023 data from the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA), 1,389 trucks and covered vans and 370 pickups were among the 7,837 vehicles involved in road accidents, nearly 22 percent of the total. On Urmi Group's vehicles, each drawing carries one message: the father should drive carefully and return home safe at the end of the day. Some pictures show family stories, others a child's love for their father. The initiative draws on the "Children's Museum Project" of Japanese transport company Miyata Unyu. After a fatal road accident, the company began displaying drivers' children's drawings on its trucks. It reported that accidents fell by around 40 percent after drawings were added to 87 vehicles over six years. In 2019, the project became an independent organization and spread to many companies across Japan. In Bangladesh, painting pictures, slogans and artwork on the back of trucks is a long-standing tradition. Urmi Group is using this familiar space to build an emotional bond between drivers and their families. The group also believes the drawings will carry a humane message to pedestrians and other drivers. Urmi Group Managing Director Asif Ashraf said he experienced the idea first-hand while attending a seminar in Japan, and it moved him personally. "A child's drawing constantly reminds a driver that a family is waiting for him to return home safely," he said. Against this […] The post Growth and innovation drive a busy year for TMAS appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: As the global textile machinery industry prepares to meet at ITMA ASIA in Shanghai this November, Swedish textile technology companies are responding to a rapidly changing market with investment, innovation and new solutions. Growing competition from Asia, geopolitical uncertainty, new regulations and the accelerating impact of AI and digitalisation are reshaping the industry. Against this backdrop, TMAS members have had a busy 2026, with new facilities, product launches and technologies addressing automation, productivity, recycling and more resource-efficient textile manufacturing. Following a record 2025 and a number of bolt-on acquisitions, ACG Kinna has inaugurated a 1,000-square-metre expansion at its headquarters in Skene in response to growing demand for its complete textile and finished product line automation services. Imogo, a pioneer in industrial spray dyeing, has opened a new showroom, test centre and production hub in Kinnahult. Imogo introduced its first Dye-Max prototype in 2019 and completed its first industrial-scale installation in 2021. The new facility now enables brands and manufacturers to move from laboratory development to validated commercial production in one location. The centre features Imogo’s patented spray application technology, combining the Mini-Max laboratory system with a fully operational industrial-scale Dye-Max line for fabrics up to 2.4 metres wide and a production capacity of approximately 3 tons per day. Using as little as 0.7 litres of dye liquor per kilogram of fabric, Dye-Max delivers major reductions in water, energy, chemicals and wastewater compared with conventional dyeing. The training programme was organised under the initiative of the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA), providing the participating students with […] The post NITER Students Gain Textile Technology and Industrial Exposure Through China Training Programme appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Eight students from the National Institute of Textile Engineering and Research (NITER) have successfully completed an international training programme in China, gaining practical exposure to advanced textile technologies, industrial operations, academic practices and cultural heritage. The training programme was organised under the initiative of the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA), providing the participating students with an opportunity to experience China’s advanced textile manufacturing ecosystem beyond classroom-based learning. During the programme, the students explored modern textile production systems, automation, quality control and industrial management practices. Their exposure covered several key areas of textile manufacturing, including spinning technology, woven fabric dyeing, man-made fibre dyeing, fabric structure and textile design. As part of the industrial visits, the students visited Shengshan Group (至山集团), where they observed modern woven fabric dyeing operations and industrial production processes. They also gained insights into the integrated technologies and production capabilities used in China’s advanced spinning sector. The programme also included academic and cultural sessions at Zhejiang Agriculture and Business College. The students participated in sessions covering Chinese 3D media, tea culture and tea processing, Chinese language, traditional armour culture, and artificial intelligence-driven vehicle technology. At Shaoxing Secondary Technical School, the students received hands-on exposure to traditional natural indigo dyeing and printing techniques. content: Author: Ahmed Javed Jamal, Country Manager, Silkflex Bangladesh Limited How a screen-printing unit uses energy, how low-cure chemicals help, which savings are evidence-backed , and what to do first. Bangladesh has 883 textile printing units, and in most of them the largest energy user is the conveyor dryer or tunnel oven at the end of the line. Many of those units also deal with unreliable power, so every kilowatt-hour and every cubic meter of gas counts. Photo: Ahmed Javed Jamal, Country Manager, Silkflex Bangladesh Limited Published energy data for screen printing alone is thin, because most Bangladeshi studies cover the garment and textile sector as a whole. This article draws on that sector evidence, technical literature, patents and supplier claims. Where a figure comes from a vendor or a patent, it is flagged. Part 1: The production process, and where the energy goes Pigment printing is the most common route for screen printing on light fabrics. Discharge printing is used mainly on dark fabrics, and rubber-based pastes are used for raised or flocked effects. Stage What happens Energy and quality points 1. Pre-treatment Fabric is scoured, bleached and prepared so it absorbs paste evenly Pretreatment quality affects hand and wash fastness. 2. Screen making Mesh is coated, dried, exposed and washed out Drying cabinets and exposure lamps. LED exposure is claimed to cut energy by 70–90% (patent). 3. Paste preparation Binder and thickener, pigment and, where needed, a fixer such as Oxal are mixed One overview lists binder with thickener, pigment, and a fixing agent for prints that are later acid- or enzyme-washed. title: Denim Deal, United Repair Centre partner to scale circular denim
summary: Denim Deal has partnered with United Repair Centre (URC) to make garment repair a larger part of circular denim strategies. The partnership gives Denim Deal members access to URC’s European repair net...
content: Denim Deal has partnered with United Repair Centre (URC) to make garment repair a larger part of circular denim strategies. The partnership gives Denim Deal members access to URC’s European repair network and a member discount. Figure: Denim Deal aims to produce 1 billion pairs of jeans containing at least 20% post-consumer recycled cotton by 2030. The collaboration connects recycled cotton with longer garment life, two critical elements of denim circularity. Denim Deal aims to produce 1 billion pairs of jeans containing at least 20% post-consumer recycled cotton by 2030. The initiative also focuses on transparency, durability and circular production across major global regions. URC brings an established repair network to the partnership. Since launching in Amsterdam in 2022, it has completed more than 100,000 repairs for over 35 brands. Its workforce includes 50+ repair technicians across Amsterdam, London and Paris. Its brand partners include Patagonia, The North Face, Arc’teryx, Lululemon, Levi’s and Decathlon.Laura Vicaria, Program Director at Denim Deal, said durability connects material choice, design, repair and future recycling. The economic potential is also significant. A Circular Fashion Federation study found that Europe’s first-hand apparel “reinvent” segment could reach €71 billion, or about $80.9 billion, by 2030. Keeping jeans in use longer through durable design and professional repair can create another value pathway before recycling.

title: CISUTAC helps advance textile circularity
title_ko: CISUTAC은 섬유 순환성을 향상시키는 데 도움을 줍니다.
summary: The CISUTAC project has concluded after four years of work across the European textile value chain, releasing a package of technologies, open data, consumer research and policy recommendations designed to support the transition towards a circular textile and clothing sector. The final results were presented on 22 and 23 September at the ECOSYSTEX Conference in […] The post CISUTAC helps advance textile circularity appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: The CISUTAC project has concluded after four years of work across the European textile value chain, releasing a package of technologies, open data, consumer research and policy recommendations designed to support the transition towards a circular textile and clothing sector. The final results were presented on 22 and 23 September at the ECOSYSTEX Conference in Antwerp, where project partners outlined progress in repair, disassembly, recycling, consumer behaviour and policy development. CISUTAC tested new repair, disassembly and recycling technologies under real operating conditions. These included methods to significantly reduce the time needed for full zipper repairs, automated disassembly systems for difficult-to-recycle protective equipment and trials showing that recycled fibres can be spun into yarns with sufficient strength for use in new garments. The project has also produced open tools and datasets intended to make textile sorting faster and more consistent. Alongside the technical work, CISUTAC carried out large-scale consumer research supported by national awareness campaigns and local guidelines. The aim was to identify the factors influencing decisions to repair, reuse and purchase second-hand textiles, while exploring ways of encouraging more circular consumption habits. Policy work formed the third major strand of the project. Assessments of possible future scenarios for the European textile sector were used to develop recommendations covering waste management, public procurement, ecodesign, standardisation and Extended Producer Responsibility. title_ko: Primark, Circ 재활용 폴리에스터 장기 계약 체결
summary: Primark has signed a multi-year offtake agreement with US textile recycler Circ for recycled polyester produced from textile waste, with the material expected to enter the retailer’s clothing ranges from 2029. The agreement is Primark’s first long-term offtake commitment with a textile-to-textile recycler and is intended to support Circ as it moves its polycotton recycling […] The post Primark signs long-term deal for Circ recycled polyester appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Primark has signed a multi-year offtake agreement with US textile recycler Circ for recycled polyester produced from textile waste, with the material expected to enter the retailer’s clothing ranges from 2029. The agreement is Primark’s first long-term offtake commitment with a textile-to-textile recycler and is intended to support Circ as it moves its polycotton recycling technology to industrial scale. Circ, headquartered in Danville, Virginia, is currently developing its first industrial-scale recycling facility in France. The plant will process textile feedstock sourced internationally, including post-consumer and post-industrial waste from Europe, and will supply the recycled polyester covered by the Primark agreement. The volumes involved and financial terms of the agreement have not been disclosed. Circ’s patented process addresses one of the persistent problems in textile recycling – separating the polyester and cellulosic components of blended polycotton fabrics so that both can be recovered as raw materials for new textiles. The company produces two main outputs, Circ Polyester and Circ Lyocell, and has already worked with fashion brands on applications for the materials. The Primark agreement, however, represents a longer-term commitment to future commercial volumes as Circ builds up its production capacity. Peter Majeranowski, CEO of Circ, said long-term commitments from major fashion retailers would be important in moving textile-to-textile recycling from demonstration and early commercial projects towards large-scale production. For Primark, the agreement forms part of efforts to increase its use of recycled fibres and reduce its dependence on virgin polyester. title: How Much Will Fashion Let AI Decide?
summary: Our data shows that fashion’s use of AI is outpacing its willingness to trust it with important choices. But technology vendors see a clear progression from assisting to automating decision-making, paired with a move away from traditional interfaces. What is fashion comfortable letting AI decide today, and how fast is that frontier likely to move? The post How Much Will Fashion Let AI Decide? appeared first on The Interline .
content: Hey, welcome back to The Interline Podcast. Right now, fashion has a laser focus on product outcomes, and for good reason. The headline research tells us that industry growth is slowing down, which means brands are competing with one another for relative rather than absolute advantage. If you listened to our recent Mailroom episode , you heard Hannah Crump from BoF Insights talk about the fact that, in a low-growth environment like the one we’re living in, you can grow your slice of the pie by subtracting it from somebody else’s, but the overall dish isn’t getting any bigger. That makes optimising per-product profitability and reducing product- and collection-level risk essential. The data also shows that consumers are way less aligned with brands than they have been in a while, and tend to make selections based on specific products instead. That makes subjective attributes like style and fit, again on an individual product or small-collection basis, matter a lot. It makes more calculated, objective criteria like pricing, value, market positioning and market counter-positioning matter arguably even more when fashion companies make the choices that bring products to market. None of these outcomes just happens. Each is the result of a set of nested decisions that cascade down from ‘This is what we want to make, given the market conditions we’ve been handed’ to the granular choices that influence how that thing gets made, how effectively it meets its objectives and how it delivers its outcomes. Each of those decisions is also, especially right now, a target for potential automation. summary: 오는 10월 3일, 1.5만명의 러너들이 효성티앤씨 리사이클 소재인 '리젠 아스킨'을 입고 달린다. 효성티앤씨는 10월 3일 인천 영종도 왕산마리나항에서 열리는 대규모 러닝 행사 ‘SMTOWN RUN CLUB 26’에 공식 의류 스폰서로 참여한다고 1일 알렸다.리사이클 기능성 섬유로 제작한 러닝 티셔츠를 선보이고 현장 체험 부스를 운영하며 약 1만5천 명의 러너와 직접 만난다.공식 러닝 티셔츠에는 효성티앤씨의 리사이클 기능성 폴리에스터 섬유 ‘regen™ ASKIN(리젠 아스킨)’을 적용했다. 리젠 아스킨은 냉감 효과와 흡한속건,

title: RoSCTL Scheme Extended for Textile Exports Until December 31
summary: The Ministry of Textiles has extended the Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) Scheme for exports of apparel, garments and made-ups by another three months until December 31. According to the ministry, the scheme has been extended from October 1 to December 31 at the existing rates and under the prevailing guidelines.
